items.title: KV cache manager metrics multiply get() results by the block size (hit rate 1600% with 16-token blocks)
items.author: wguo7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`KVCacheManager.get()` returns the number of tokens it fetched ([cache_manager.py#L1135-L1137](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/4d1d0c06b07a341eccc9bb0a7231d1d161f60907/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/cache_manager.py#L1135-L1137)). The metrics recorder treats an `int` GET result as a number of blocks and multiplies it by `block_ntokens` ([metrics.py#L243-L249](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/4d1d0c06b07a341eccc9bb0a7231d1d161f60907/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/metrics.py#L243-L249) for fetched tokens, [metrics.py#L560-L566](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/4d1d0c06b07a341eccc9bb0a7231d1d161f60907/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/metrics.py#L560-L566) for hits and misses). That scaling is right for `L2Cache.get()`, which returns blocks, but `KVCacheMetrics` gives the manager's metrics the same `block_ntokens` ([metrics.py#L793-L798](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/4d1d0c06b07a341eccc9bb0a7231d1d161f60907/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/metrics.py#L793-L798)), so each manager `get()` is counted `block_ntokens` times over.

With 16-token blocks, a `get()` that fetches all 64 requested tokens is logged as 1024 hits and -960 misses, a hit rate of 1600%. The fetched-token count recorded for the manager's GET op, which feeds its exported fetched-tokens histogram, is 1024 as well.

`acquire()` returns a `(tokens, handle)` tuple, which the recorder reads without scaling, so `acquire()` is counted correctly. The bundled vLLM connectors call `acquire()`, so only code that calls `get()` directly sees the wrong numbers.

### Steps to Reproduce

The script puts 64 tokens (4 blocks of 16) into a manager with an L1 cache on the CPU, gets them back with `get()`, and prints the manager's metrics. Output on main (4d1d0c0):

```
get() returned 64 tokens (requested 64)
actual: mgr hit=1024 miss=-960 fetched=[1024]
expected: mgr hit=64 miss=0 fetched=[64]
summary: Num. of hit: 1024, Num. of miss: -960, Hit rate: 1600.00%
```

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""KVCacheManager.get() hit/miss metrics are multiplied by block_ntokens.

Run: KVCACHE_SRC=<aibrix>/python/aibrix_kvcache python -u repro.py
L1 cache on CPU only; no GPU or L2 backend needed.
"""

import os
import sys
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
for k in [k for k in os.environ if k.startswith("AIBRIX_")]:
    del os.environ[k]
os.environ["AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L1_CACHE_ENABLED"] = "1"
os.environ["AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L2_CACHE_BACKEND"] = ""
os.environ["AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L1_CACHE_CAPACITY_GB"] = "0.001"
os.environ["AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L1_CACHE_DEVICE"] = "cpu"
os.environ["AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L1_CACHE_PIN_MEMORY"] = "0"
sys.path.insert(0, os.environ.get("KVCACHE_SRC", "."))

import torch  # noqa: E402

from aibrix_kvcache import (  # noqa: E402
    BaseKVCacheManager,
    KVCacheBlockLayout,
    KVCacheBlockSpec,
    KVCacheConfig,
    KVCacheTensorSpec,
    ModelSpec,
    TokenListView,
    cache_manager,
)
from aibrix_kvcache.memory import TensorPoolAllocator  # noqa: E402

cache_manager.TESTING_DISABLE_PIN_MEMORY = True
BLK = 16
spec = KVCacheBlockSpec(
    block_ntokens=BLK,
    block_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    block_layout=KVCacheBlockLayout.NCLD,
    tensor_spec=KVCacheTensorSpec(heads=[1, 2], layers=list(range(8)), head_size=32),
)
TensorPoolAllocator.SLAB_MAX_NBYTES = spec.block_nbytes * 64
mgr = BaseKVCacheManager(config=KVCacheConfig(block_spec=spec, model_spec=ModelSpec(1024)))

tokens = TokenListView(list(range(4 * BLK)))  # 4 full blocks = 64 tokens

h = mgr.allocate_for(None, tokens).get()
assert mgr.put(None, tokens, h).is_ok()

get_handle = mgr.allocate_for(None, tokens).get()
st = mgr.get(None, tokens, get_handle)
get_handle.release()
print(f"get() returned {st.get()} tokens (requested {len(tokens)})")

m = mgr.metrics.mgr
print(f"actual: mgr hit={m.num_tokens_hit} miss={m.num_tokens_miss} "
      f"fetched={m.get_metrics.num_fetched_tokens}")
print(f"expected: mgr hit={len(tokens)} miss=0 fetched=[{len(tokens)}]")
print("summary: Num. of hit" + m.summary().split("Num. of hit")[-1].rstrip())
mgr.close()
os._exit(0)
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

The manager's metrics count 64 hits, 0 misses and 64 fetched tokens for that `get()`.

### Environment

- AIBrix version: main at 4d1d0c0
- Deployment environment: none. The repro runs `aibrix_kvcache` in-process on the CPU (macOS arm64, Python 3.12.15, torch 2.14.1)
- LLM(s) being used: none

### Area

KV Cache

I have a fix with a test ready and will open a PR.

items.title: [Feature]: VisualGen MiniMax-H3: support AdaLN-pruned checkpoints (multimodalart/MiniMax-H3-Pruned)
items.author: atokayev
items.body_excerpt:
### The feature, motivation and pitch

Please add support for the community AdaLN-pruned MiniMax-H3 checkpoint ([multimodalart/MiniMax-H3-Pruned](https://huggingface.co/multimodalart/MiniMax-H3-Pruned)) in the VisualGen MiniMax-H3 pipeline.

**Motivation.** The pruned transformer is 40 GiB instead of 66 GiB (39% fewer parameters), and the text encoder is truncated from 66.7 to 52.5 GB. In diffusers this makes MiniMax-H3 fit one 80 GB H100 (see below), which the stock checkpoint cannot do in VisualGen today (weights alone are about 104 GiB with an FP8 transformer, and there is no CPU offload for H3; see #13893).

**Current behavior (1.3.0rc29, 1x H200).** `VisualGen(model=<dir>)` detects the MiniMax-H3 pipeline and reads the weights, then `MiniMaxH3Transformer.load_weights` fails:

```
ValueError: MiniMax-H3 checkpoint is missing 55 required tensors:
time_embedder.linear_1.weight, time_embedder.linear_1.bias,
time_embedder.linear_2.weight, time_embedder.linear_2.bias,
transformer_blocks.0.adaln_proj.linear.bias, ...
  tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/models/minimax_h3/transformer_minimax_h3.py:859
```

**Why.** The pruned checkpoint stores AdaLN differently:

| | Stock | Pruned |
|---|---|---|
| Time embedding | `time_embedder.linear_1/2` (MLP) | `time_embedder.table` (precomputed, 1025 entries) |
| `adaln_proj.linear.weight` | (96768, 2688) | (96768, 8) |
| `adaln_proj` bias | `adaln_proj.linear.bias` | `adaln_proj.folded_bias` |
| Extra tensors | none | `adaln_basis` [8, 2688], `adaln_mean` [2688] (in `transformer/adaln_affine.safetensors`) |
| Transformer config | stock | custom class `MiniMaxH3PrunedTransformer3DModel` (`auto_map`), `adaln_rank: 8`, `num_layers: 50` |

The reference implementation is `modeling_minimax_h3_pruned.py` in the pruned repo. Expanding the weights back to the stock shapes would make the loader pass but restores the 66 GiB transformer, so it does not help. The useful change is a rank-8 AdaLN and time-table path in the transformer.

**Reproduction.**
1. Build a model directory with the stock `vae`, `scheduler`, `audio_scheduler`, `audio_vae`, `tokenizer`, `processor` and `modular_model_index.json` from `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`, and the `transformer/` and `text_encoder/` from `multimodalart/MiniMax-H3-Pruned`.
2. Run `VisualGen(model=<dir>, args=VisualGenArgs.from_yaml("cfg.yaml"))` with `quant_config: {quant_algo: FP8, dynamic: true}`, `attention_config: {backend: FA4}`, resolution 480x832, 124 frames.

**Measured with the pruned weights in diffusers** (modular pipeline, 832x480, 124 frames, 28 steps, seed 42, 8 prompts, 1x H200):
- Cost: 9.5 GPU-s per video-s vs 20.9 for the stock checkpoint, both with CPU offload (2.2x). This is not a comparison with TensorRT-LLM.
- Quality vs stock: VBench composite +0.003 (95% paired-bootstrap interval -0.000 to +0.006); LPIPS 0.146, similar to the 0.149 between two stock runs on different engines. Only 8 prompts and one seed.
- Memory on an emulated 80 GB H100 (driver-reported free memory capped; real H100 not tested): peak 52.6 GiB at 960x544 and 53.4 GiB at 1344x768 with automatic CPU offload. The stock checkpoint peaks at 76.8 GiB there.

### Alternatives

- **CPU offload in VisualGen (#13893):** would also help H100 fit, but costs latency; pruning shrinks the weights themselves.
- **Quantized pruned variants** (SDNQ, GGUF, NVFP4 builds exist on Hugging Face) use formats VisualGen does not load.
- **Converter to the stock layout:** loads, but gives back the full transformer size.

### Additional context

- Related: #13893 (offloading for visual_gen) and the open PR #19772 (fuses MiniMax-H3 AdaLN RMSNorm with per-token modulation), which touches the same AdaLN code a pruned path would change.
- Open question: does the truncated 51-layer text encoder load in VisualGen? The failure occurs before that point.
- The FastH3 4-step adapter also expects the original AdaLN width, so we have not tested pruned + distilled in any engine.
- Environment: TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29 (NGC image), 1x H200, includes the MiniMax-H3 support from #18733.

<details>
<summary>Trimmed log (TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29, 1x H200)</summary>

```
[TensorRT-LLM] TensorRT LLM version: 1.3.0rc29
Loading transformer: 100%|██████████| 15/15
Loading MiniMax-H3 weights: ...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/executor.py", line 820, in run_diffusion_worker
    executor = DiffusionExecutor(
  File ".../tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/executor.py", line 486, in __init__
    self._load_pipeline()
  File ".../tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/executor.py", line 521, in _load_pipeline
    self.pipeline = loader.load(
  File ".../tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/pipeline_loader.py", line 305, in load
    pipeline.load_weights(weights)
  File ".../tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/models/minimax_h3/pipeline_minimax_h3.py", line 237, in load_weights

  File ".../tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/models/minimax_h3/transformer_minimax_h3.py", line 859, in load_weights

ValueError: MiniMax-H3 checkpoint is missing 55 required tensors: time_embedder.linear_1.weight, time_embedder.linear_1.bias, time_embedder.linear_2.weight, time_embedder.linear_2.bias, transformer_blocks.0.adaln_proj.linear.bias, transformer_blocks.1.adaln_proj.linear.bias, transformer_blocks.2.adaln_proj.linear.bias, transformer_blocks.3.adaln_proj.linear.bias ...

items.title: [Feature]: Whisper serving parity in trtllm-serve — /v1/audio/transcriptions, long-form audio, verbose_json segments, decoder biasing
items.author: ravo42-maker
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`openai/whisper-large-v3` runs on the PyTorch backend once the pending KV-cache fixes land (#19302 for #18609 / #19515, #19516 for #19514), and the engine itself is fast: on an RTX 5070 Ti, fp16, 0.34 s per 30 s clip warm (~87x realtime; ~14x for faster-whisper large-v3 float32 on the same clip). But it is still not usable as a drop-in STT service, because the serving layer is missing. Our use case is clinical dictation (10–20 minute recordings), currently served by faster-whisper and vLLM; every gap below is something those two already provide. Ordered by how blocking it is:

1. **`/v1/audio/transcriptions` (and `/v1/audio/translations`) in `trtllm-serve`.** Today audio reaches the model only through `/v1/chat/completions` with `input_audio` or the Python `LLM` API. Every OpenAI-compatible STT client uses the audio route: multipart `file`, `model`, `language`, `prompt`, `temperature`, `response_format`, `timestamp_granularities`. Nothing under `tensorrt_llm/serve/` implements it on current `main`.

2. **Long-form audio.** `WhisperInputProcessor` accepts exactly one clip of at most `max_source_positions` (1500 frames = 30 s) and rejects longer input with "chunk the audio" (`modeling_whisper.py`, the `max_audio_seconds` check). A 16-minute file needs windowing on the server, ideally seek-based — the next window starts at the last complete segment's end timestamp, as openai/whisper and faster-whisper do. Fixed pre-cut 30 s chunks lose words at mid-sentence cuts (vllm-project/vllm#58029 documents that failure mode), so this depends on item 3.

3. **`verbose_json` output: per-segment `start`/`end`, `text`, `avg_logprob`, `compression_ratio`** (and `no_speech_prob` where available). The input processor currently forces `<|notimestamps|>` in the decoder prompt, so timestamps are never produced. Per-segment `compression_ratio` is what production pipelines use to detect Whisper's repetition loops; without it the service cannot be monitored.

4. **Decoder biasing:** `prompt` (previous-text conditioning across windows) and a `hotwords`-style bias for proper nouns. faster-whisper exposes both; vLLM accepts `hotwords`.

5. **Whisper-specific input validation.** A user-supplied `max_seq_len` below `max_source_positions` should be rejected: with `max_batch_size=2` it fails at the micro-batch scheduler, but with `max_batch_size=8` it passes and silently drops phrases from the transcript (details in #19514).

Items 1 and 3 are the ones that would let a maintainer or contributor close the gap to vLLM's `/v1/audio/transcriptions`; 2 builds on 3; 4 and 5 are independent.

### Alternatives

A thin service in front of the `LLM` API that does windowing, emits segment timestamps and emulates the OpenAI response shape. That duplicates what vLLM already ships and every TensorRT-LLM Whisper user would have to write it.

### Additional context

Hardware verification runs, the rc25 + patch wheel and the repro kit are described in #18609, #19450, #19514, #19515, #19516 and in the #19302 thread. Happy to test any of the above on sm_120 and on real multi-minute dictations.

items.title: Fused fprop scale/bias iterator advances without the split-k factor and drifts from activation channels
items.author: VaggelisGian
items.body_excerpt:
### Description

In the fused (scale/bias) fprop mainloop, the scale/bias vector iterator and the activation/filter iterators disagree on the per-R*S-cycle channel stride when `split_k_slices > 1`, so scale/bias drift to the wrong channel blocks.

- Activation iterator on gemm-k wrap (include/cutlass/conv/threadblock/conv2d_fprop_activation_tile_access_iterator_analytic.h ~line 216, `_optimized` analogue ~314): `filter_c_ += Shape::kColumn * problem_size_.split_k_slices;`
- Scale/bias iterator on the same wrap (include/cutlass/conv/threadblock/predicated_scale_bias_vector_access_iterator.h:247-262): calls `add_tile_offset(TensorCoord(1, 0))`, which advances by a single `ThreadblockShape::kContiguous`, with no split-k factor.

Both start consistently at channel `threadblock_tile_idx.k() * kK` (implicit_gemm_convolution_fusion.h ~296-337), so the divergence accumulates once the loop wraps past R*S. With interleaved slice partitioning, each additional R*S cycle applies bias/scale from one kK-block earlier than the channels the activations actually carry. This needs `split_k_slices > 1` and more than one C-channel block per slice (`ceil(ceil(C/S)/kK) >= 2`) to appear, e.g. split_k_slices=4, C=256, ThreadblockShape::kK=32, R*S>=2: from the second cycle on, bias[64+j*32] is applied where the activations come from channels 192+. The result is silent wrong numerics, not an OOB.

The same pattern exists in the conv3d fusion headers (conv3d_fprop_activation_tile_access_iterator_analytic/_optimized vs the shared scale/bias iterator). Wgrad fusion is unaffected: it loads scale/bias once, with no per-tile advance.

The device layer explicitly supports split-k for fused fprop (workspace handling in include/cutlass/conv/device/implicit_gemm_convolution_fusion.h ~148-175), so the combination is reachable through the public API.

This finding is from static verification of the two advance paths; I have not built an end-to-end failing kernel, but the stride mismatch is exactly the missing `split_k_slices` factor and the start offsets agree.

### Suggested fix

Multiply the scale/bias iterator's wrap stride by `problem_size.split_k_slices` in `advance()`, mirroring the activation iterators.

items.title: [BUG] Example 77 MLA fused split-KV reduction (--fuse_reduction) can hang or return wrong output
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CUTLASS C++

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

**Summary.** In the Blackwell MLA example's fused split-KV reduction (`--fuse_reduction`, `split_kv > 1`), the counter wait that synchronizes the split CTAs in `epilogue_lse_reduction` can hang the whole split group, and can let peer CTAs read the LSE exchange buffers before every contribution has landed, which gives wrong output. File: `examples/77_blackwell_fmha/kernel/sm100_fmha_mla_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`, lambda at lines 1952–1960, called at 1971 and 1981. #3763 fixes both by building the wait from `cutlass::GenericBarrier`'s `arrive_inc` and `wait_lt`.

#### Cause

Below, S is `local_split_kv`, the group's number of non-empty splits (at most `--split_kv`).

- **Overtaken equality wait (hang).** Phase 1 spins until `atomicCAS(lock, count, count)` returns exactly S (line 1956). A CTA that has already passed can add its phase-2 increment before a slower peer polls again; the slower peer then never sees S and never adds its own phase-2 increment, so the counter stops below 2S and every CTA of the group spins forever.
- **Arrival before contribution (wrong output).** Thread 0 increments the counter without waiting for the CTA's other contributing threads (in practice warp 1 of the 2-SM kernel): the lambda's only barrier comes after the spin, and a `__threadfence()` publishes only writes already in the fencing thread's causality past. A peer that sees the count can then read the LSE max (1973) before warp 1's `atomicMax` lands, or the LSE sum (1983) before its `atomicAdd` lands.

#### Suggested fix

See #3763. `arrive_inc` syncs the compute warps before thread 0's release increment, and `wait_lt` has thread 0 wait with an acquire load until the counter is at least the target.

#### Scope

- Affected: only `--fuse_reduction` with `split_kv > 1`; `is_fused_reduction` defaults to false (`77_blackwell_mla.cu`, line 87). The default split-KV path uses the separate `Sm100FmhaMlaReductionKernel` and is not affected. The lambda is unchanged from v4.2.0 to main `91843b7`.
- Evidence, from `77_blackwell_mla_2sm_fp16` on a B300 that was time-shared with another user's job (details and method in #3763):
  - Hang without any injected delay: 13 of 18 stress processes (1001 back-to-back launches each, six configurations with `--split_kv` 8 to 64) hung until killed at 300 s. With only a watchdog added to the same wait, every hang burst (1108 over 13 of 18 processes) contains a CTA waiting for exactly S that read a counter value above S. The `TEST_MLA_FUSE_REDUCTION` configuration (b=1, `--split_kv` 8) did not hang in 3 of 3 processes.
  - Hang under a forced legal schedule (thread 0 of one split waits 100 µs before each phase-1 poll): 60 of 60 runs, with peers waiting for 2S and the counter at 2S − 1.
  - Wrong output only under a forced legal schedule (warp 1 of one split waits 100 µs before its phase-2 `atomicAdd`): 60 of 60 runs fail `--verify`. Apart from near-threshold misses at `--split_kv` 64, which are a separate numerical issue (see #3763), we have not seen wrong output without a delay; a stress process verifies only its last launch.
- With #3763: none of 18 stress processes hung (18,018 launches). With its barrier inlined into our test patch, neither forced schedule hung or produced a race failure in 60 runs; 3 of them missed the 1e-2 threshold with max diff 0.0117, the size of the numerical misses, against 0.2 or more for every race failure.

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

Unmodified example, built with CMake `-DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS=103a`, on a B300:

```
./77_blackwell_mla_2sm_fp16 --b=8 --k=8192 --split_kv=20 --page=128 --fuse_reduction --verify --iterations=1000
```

Expected: the process finishes and `--verify` passes. Actual: it hung in 3 of 3 attempts until killed at 300 s.

The wrong output needs one late warp: a 100 µs `%globaltimer` busy-wait in warp 1 of one split per group, placed just before the `atomicAdd` at line 1979, makes `--verify` report "failed O" in every run.

**Expected behavior**

The fused reduction completes and matches the reference however the split CTAs are scheduled.

**Environment details (please complete the following information):**
 - Environment location: Bare-metal. NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, driver 610.57.04, CUDA 12.9, CUTLASS `0b55a2f` (the file is byte-identical on main `91843b7`). The GPU was time-shared with another user's job during the runs.

items.title: Improve the error message in `linalg.eigh` when using large matrices
items.author: gabitza-tech
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

I am using eigh() function from torch.linalg liberary on a [53000,53000] matrix.

```python
def eigDecompose(
    laplacian: torch.Tensor, cuda: bool, device: torch.device = torch.device('cpu')
) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors from the Laplacian matrix.
    """
    if cuda:
        if device is None:
            device = torch.cuda.current_device()
        laplacian = laplacian.float().to(device)
    else:
        laplacian = laplacian.float()
    lambdas, diffusion_map = eigh(laplacian)
    return lambdas, diffusion_map

```

I get the following error:
> Intel MKL ERROR: Parameter 8 was incorrect on entry to SSYEVD.
> [...]
> laplacian = laplacian.float()
>     lambdas, diffusion_map = eigh(laplacian)
>                              ~~~~ <--- HERE
>     return lambdas, diffusion_map
> RuntimeError: false INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at "/opt/conda/conda-bld/pytorch_1666642865319/work/aten/src/ATen/native/BatchLinearAlgebra.cpp":1462, please report a bug to PyTorch. linalg.eigh: Argument 8 has illegal value. Most certainly there is a bug in the implementation calling the backend library.

You can reproduce the error:
>>>import torch as t
>>>t.linalg.eigh(t.randn([53000,53000])).detach()
>>>
>>>Intel MKL ERROR: Parameter 8 was incorrect on entry to SSYEVD.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
RuntimeError: false INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at "/opt/conda/conda-bld/pytorch_1666642865319/work/aten/src/ATen/native/BatchLinearAlgebra.cpp":1462, please report a bug to PyTorch. linalg.eigh: Argument 8 has illegal value. Most certainly there is a bug in the implementation calling the backend library.

Is there a way to split the matrix in smaller parts, calculate the eigh(), merge them and get the same result? From what I understood, the size is bigger than INT32 upper limit.




### Versions

PyTorch built with:
  - GCC 9.3
  - C++ Version: 201402
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Math Kernel Library Version 2021.4-Product Build 20210904 for Intel(R) 64 architecture applications
  - Intel(R) MKL-DNN v2.6.0 (Git Hash 52b5f107dd9cf10910aaa19cb47f3abf9b349815)

comments.author: IvanYashchuk
comments.body:
For `n=53000` the `lwork` argument of [`ssyevd`](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/develop/documentation/onemkl-developer-reference-fortran/top/lapack-routines/lapack-least-squares-and-eigenvalue-problem/lapack-least-squares-eigenvalue-problem-driver/symmetric-eigenvalue-problems-lapack-driver/syevd.html) must be ≥ 2*n^2+ 6*n + 1, which a lot larger than 32bit-interface that we are using can handle.
We should raise a better error message, this part is simple - introduce a check here:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/aten/src/ATen/native/BatchLinearAlgebraKernel.cpp#L261

Supporting these large matrices is possible, but requires implementing https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/51720.

comments.body: As you're computing on CPU, I suggest using NumPy with the 64-bit build of LAPACK: https://numpy.org/devdocs/user/building.html#bit-blas-and-lapack. Wrapping that `numpy.linalg.eigh` call into `torch.autograd.Function` with a custom derivative is not complicated. It's of course unfortunate.

items.title: [symm_mem] Free NCCL backing only after its windows are deregistered
items.author: jackLei0901
items.body_excerpt:
Following up on [@fduwjj’s teardown diagnosis](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/200738#issuecomment-6155641311).

On main `4f3ee7aa3708`, [`free()`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/4f3ee7aa37084ba2469f05430db08ce449f3e206/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/NCCLSymmetricMemory.cu#L593-L606) drops cached handles, then erases the allocation. [`~NCCLAllocation`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/4f3ee7aa37084ba2469f05430db08ce449f3e206/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/NCCLSymmetricMemory.cu#L63-L74) calls `ncclMemFree` before its [`peer_alloc_infos_` member](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/4f3ee7aa37084ba2469f05430db08ce449f3e206/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/NCCLSymmetricMemory.cu#L50-L51) is destroyed and the peer infos [deregister their windows](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/4f3ee7aa37084ba2469f05430db08ce449f3e206/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/NCCLSymmetricMemory.cu#L291).

Even without an external handle, the allocation’s map holds the remaining peer-info references, so deregistration follows the backing free. Retaining a handle can delay deregistration further.

I propose a shared backing owner retained by both the allocation and its peer infos. With the communicator still valid, each peer info would deregister its window before releasing its backing reference. This would also keep backing alive for retained handles, following the CUDA backend’s [`AllocationRef` ownership pattern](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/4f3ee7aa37084ba2469f05430db08ce449f3e206/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/CUDASymmetricMemory.hpp#L83).

Destroyed-communicator handling, concurrent teardown, and cache unification would stay out of scope. This report is based on source inspection and the existing diagnosis; I have not independently reproduced the failure or started implementing a fix.

@fduwjj, is anyone already working on this? If not, would you approve this scope and assign the issue to me? Is retaining backing for external handles the intended contract, and should this wait for or be coordinated with [#200703](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/200703)? After scope approval, I can arrange two-GPU validation.

AI tools assisted with source inspection and drafting.

cc @awgu @wanchaol @fegin @fduwjj @wz337 @wconstab @d4l3k @pragupta @msaroufim @dcci @aditvenk @weifengpy @kapilsh

items.title: Bug Report: Segfault in torch.xpu.is_available() on WSL3 + Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage) despite ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=0
items.author: Arch-Gemini
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Description
Calling torch.xpu.is_available() causes an immediate segmentation fault on WSL3 with Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage). The crash occurs inside _enum_zes_device_infos() during device enumeration. Setting ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=0 and ZE_ENABLE_SYSMAN=0 has no effect — PyTorch appears to hardcode the Sysman initialization path and ignores these environment variables.
Environment
PyTorch Version: 2.14.1+xpu (pip)
Python Version: 3.14
OS: Ubuntu Resolute (WSL3, kernel via /dev/dxg)
GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage)
Windows Host Driver: 32.0.101.9150 (2026-10-08) ✅ Latest
oneAPI / Level Zero: Bundled via pip (intel-sycl-rt, pyzes)
Installation Method: pip (--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu)
Steps to Reproduce
bash

编辑



export ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=0
export ZE_ENABLE_SYSMAN=0
python -X faulthandler -c "import torch; print(torch.xpu.is_available())"
Actual Behavior
文本

编辑



/mnt/c/Users/Administrator/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/torch/xpu/__init__.py:251: UserWarning: Can't initialize Level Zero Sysman
  return _enum_zes_device_infos(visible_mask)
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

Current thread 0x00007add107171c0 [python] (most recent call first):
  File ".../torch/xpu/__init__.py", line 278 in device_count
  File ".../torch/xpu/__init__.py", line 290 in is_available
  File "<string>", line 1 in <module>

Current thread's C stack trace (most recent call first):
  Binary file "python", at _Py_DumpStack+0x4a [0x47728a]
  Binary file "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6", at +0x45cb0 [0x7add10445cb0]
Expected Behavior
torch.xpu.is_available() should either:
Successfully detect the XPU device, OR
Respect ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=0 and gracefully fall back to non-Sysman enumeration, returning True or False without crashing.
Additional Context
ze-info is not available in the pip-installed environment, so independent Level Zero validation was not possible.
The Windows driver (32.0.101.9150) is the latest release and fully supports Battlemage.
The segfault occurs specifically in _enum_zes_device_infos(), suggesting the WSL3 /dev/dxg Sysman IOCTL for Battlemage may return unexpected data that PyTorch does not handle safely.
This is a hard crash (SIGSEGV), not a Python exception — it cannot be caught with try/except.
Suggested Fix
Make Sysman initialization respect ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=0 at the C++ binding level.
Add null/bounds checking around _enum_zes_device_infos() to prevent segfaults when Sysman returns invalid data on WSL3.
Consider adding a fallback enumeration path for WSL environments where Sysman is known to be unreliable.
Labels
module: xpu, module: third_party, high priority, bug

### Versions

PyTorch Version: 2.14.1+xpu (pip)
Python Version: 3.14
OS: Ubuntu Resolute (WSL3, kernel via /dev/dxg)
GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage)
Windows Host Driver: 32.0.101.9150 (2026-10-08) ✅ Latest
oneAPI / Level Zero: Bundled via pip (intel-sycl-rt, pyzes)
Installation Method: pip (--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu)

items.title: [Bug] Prefill overload filter can never skip a hot pod with 5 or fewer prefill pods
items.author: AarnavNoble
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The overload filter that skips a hot prefill pod can never skip one in a deployment with 5 or fewer prefill pods, at the shipped `AIBRIX_PREFIX_CACHE_STANDARD_DEVIATION_FACTOR=2`.

`scorePreparedPrefillPods` (`pd/router/router.go`) skips a pod when

```
reqCnt > mean + factor × stddev
```

where `stddev` is the sample standard deviation (`routeutil.StandardDeviation`, n−1) over the pods' in-flight prefill counts. By Samuelson's inequality, no value in a set of n numbers can sit more than (n−1)/√n sample standard deviations above their mean:

| prefill pods (n) | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| max (x − mean) / stddev | 0.71 | 1.15 | 1.50 | 1.79 | 2.04 |

With factor 2, the condition is unreachable for n ≤ 5, whatever the counts. For example, with 4 pods at [12, 0, 0, 0], the mean is 3 and the stddev is 6, so the threshold is 15 and the pod with 12 in flight is not skipped. With the code's own default of 1 (`defaultStandardDeviationFactor`), it is unreachable for n = 2. The manifests and the chart (`config/gateway/gateway-plugin/gateway-plugin.yaml`, `dist/chart/values.yaml`) all ship 2.

The prefix-cache router's selection (`getTargetPodFromMatchedPodsFromCounts`) uses the same `mean + factor × stddev` bound over the ready pods, so it has the same limit.

Small prefill pools are common in PD deployments, so the filter is effectively off for many of them. A prefix-matched pod is chosen however far ahead of the others it is.

### Steps to Reproduce

The bound is arithmetic, so the table above is the reproduction. In code: give `scorePreparedPrefillPods` 4 prefill pods with in-flight counts [12, 0, 0, 0] and factor 2. The busy pod is scored, not skipped.

### Expected behavior

A prefill pod far above the others in load is skipped, whatever the pool size.

### Possible fixes

- **A. Bounded-load cap (my suggestion).** Skip a pod whose count exceeds `c × (mean + 1)` for a constant c (for example 1.25 to 2). This is the "consistent hashing with bounded loads" rule. It works at any n, and the `+1` keeps an idle pool from rejecting its first request.
- **B. Population stddev, or a per-n factor.** The population bound is √(n−1), which is still unreachable at factor 2 for n ≤ 5, so this only moves the threshold.
- **C. Document the limit.** Note in `ENV_VARS.md` and `pd_readme.md` that the factor must be below (n−1)/√n for the filter to ever apply.

I'd propose A for the PD prefill filter, keeping the env var's meaning or adding a new knob, whichever you prefer. Happy to send a PR.

### Environment

`main` at ca25b37b. PD prefill selection, and the prefix-cache router.

### Area

Gateway (PD routing, prefix cache)

items.title: [Bug] KPA asks for one extra pod when the exact replica count is a whole number
items.author: AarnavNoble
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

KPA can ask for one pod more than the load needs when the exact answer is a whole number, because of floating-point error.

`desiredPodCounts` (`algorithm/kpa.go:211,218`) computes `math.Ceil(load * observed / target)`. Multiplying first can leave the result just above the exact integer, and `Ceil` then adds a pod:

| Pods | Per-pod value | Target | `load * value / target` | KPA | Exact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 0.84 | 0.7 | 12.000000000000002 | **13** | 12 |
| 5 | 0.42 | 0.3 | 7.000000000000001 | **8** | 7 |
| 6 | 0.05 | 0.1 | 3.0000000000000004 | **4** | 3 |

APA computes `currentPodCount * (value / target)` and gets 12, 7 and 3 for the same inputs, so the two algorithms disagree on the same metric.

Ratio targets such as GPU cache usage `0.7` are common, so a steady load landing on such a value is not unusual. The extra pod is held for as long as the value stays there.

### Steps to Reproduce

`KPAAlgorithm.desiredPodCounts` with a `POD` metric source, target `0.7`, tolerance 0.1, 10 current pods, and a stable and panic value of `0.84` (parsed from a string). The result is 13.

### Expected behavior

12, the exact answer.

### Possible fix

Snap results within a small epsilon of an integer before `Ceil`, for example `math.Ceil(x - 1e-9)`, in one helper used by both windows. Reordering to `load * (observed / target)` fixes these cases but moves the error to other inputs. Add the table above as test cases. Happy to send a PR.

### Environment

`main` at 52b8834e.

### Area

Autoscaler (KPA)

items.title: Model runtime cannot download gcs:// artifact URLs that the ModelClaim API lists as supported
items.author: wguo7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

The ModelClaim API comment ([modelclaim_types.go#L62-L63](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/d638496c0f66fd4483667f15b0b55cf5c9349fa1/api/model/v1alpha1/modelclaim_types.go#L62-L63)) and the `_resolve_model_path()` docstring ([model_runtime.py#L1010](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/d638496c0f66fd4483667f15b0b55cf5c9349fa1/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/model_runtime.py#L1010)) list `gcs://` as a supported artifact URL, but the model runtime cannot download one.

`_resolve_model_path()` stages remote weights through `aibrix.downloader.download_model()`. That downloader handles S3 and TOS, and every other URL falls through to the Hugging Face downloader ([base.py#L312-L317](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/d638496c0f66fd4483667f15b0b55cf5c9349fa1/python/aibrix/aibrix/downloader/base.py#L312-L317)). A `gcs://` or `gs://` URL therefore fails with `ArgNotFormatError` ("Argument `model_uri` is not in the expected format: repo/name"), which does not mention the scheme. Until #3258 merged, this error was swallowed and the engine started with `bucket/key` as its model (#3257). It now fails at launch.

The runtime already has a GCS downloader: `aibrix/runtime/downloaders.py` maps `gcs` and `gs` to `GCSArtifactDownloader` and raises `ValueError("Unsupported URL scheme: ...")` for anything else ([downloaders.py#L649-L681](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/d638496c0f66fd4483667f15b0b55cf5c9349fa1/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/downloaders.py#L649-L681)). `artifact_service.py` uses it ([artifact_service.py#L208](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/d638496c0f66fd4483667f15b0b55cf5c9349fa1/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/artifact_service.py#L208)), but the model weight path does not.

### Steps to Reproduce

The script resolves a `gcs://` and a `gs://` URL the way the model runtime does before it starts the engine. Output on main (f3300be):

```
gcs://my-bucket/models/llama-3-8b -> ArgNotFormatError: Argument `model_uri` is not in the expected format: repo/name
gs://my-bucket/models/llama-3-8b -> ArgNotFormatError: Argument `model_uri` is not in the expected format: repo/name
```

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Run: AIBRIX_SRC=<aibrix>/python/aibrix python repro.py"""

import logging
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.environ["AIBRIX_SRC"])
logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)

from aibrix.runtime.model_runtime import _resolve_model_path  # noqa: E402

for url in ["gcs://my-bucket/models/llama-3-8b", "gs://my-bucket/models/llama-3-8b"]:
    try:
        print(url, "->", repr(_resolve_model_path(url)))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(url, "->", type(e).__name__ + ":", str(e).splitlines()[0])
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

One of:
1. `_resolve_model_path()` downloads `gcs://` and `gs://` URLs, for example through `GCSArtifactDownloader`.
2. If GCS is not meant to be supported for model weights, an unsupported scheme fails with an error that names the scheme, and the API comment and docstring stop listing `gcs://`.

Which of the two fits the project better is a maintainer call. I can send a PR for either.

### Environment

- AIBrix version: main at f3300be
- Deployment environment: none. The repro calls the runtime function in-process (macOS arm64, Python 3.12.15)
- LLM(s) being used: none

### Area

Runtime

items.title: [Tracking][MP] Native KV events: scheduler-side subscription, engine-native identities, vLLM + SGLang
items.author: DongDongJu
items.body_excerpt:
## Problem

State of `dev` (dbe22ef) after #5076, #5307, #5524. 
The data path is fine: stores and retrieves work.
What routers are told about the CPU tier is wrong in five ways.

### 1. Events carry LMCache chunk hashes; routers index engine block hashes

The MP server records an `L1_WRITE_FINISHED` per chunk and the worker turns it into `BlockStored(block_hashes=[chunk_hash], block_size=chunk_size, token_ids=<chunk tokens>)`. `chunk_hash` is LMCache's `TokenHasher` output at LMCache chunk granularity.

Routers match requests against engine identities.
llm-d's precise prefix index compares against hashes computed with vLLM's prefix-caching algorithm at the engine block size.
Dynamo rehashes `token_ids` at its configured `kv_block_size`. Either way a CPU placement is only found when the LMCache chunk equals the engine block (16 tokens) and, for llm-d, the hash algorithm and seed coincide as well.
That is the configuration #5307 was validated with (chunk size 16, unsalted sha256_cbor).
LMCache's default chunk is 256 and the chunk size sets the transfer granularity, so pinning it to 16 for routing is not a configuration we can require.
With 256-token chunks and 16-token blocks the event describes a block nobody ever queries.

A second effect: GPU events (native hashes) and CPU events (chunk hashes) for the same prefix are two unrelated hash chains.
A request whose prefix is partly on GPU and partly on CPU cannot be scored as one prefix.

### 2. Stored/Removed are per-object write/evict notifications, not a residency decision

The server emits Stored when any L1 write for a chunk finishes and Removed when any L1 key for it is evicted.
With TP>1 a chunk is one object per `(kv_rank, object_group)`; with multiple L1 tags the same object can have several copies.
So the router can be told a prefix is on CPU while other ranks' objects are still in flight (routing there gives a partial hit and a recompute), and told it is gone while another copy is still readable (#5694 — lost hits).

### 3. Placements go stale while the engine is idle

vLLM drains `connector.take_events()` only inside `Scheduler.update_from_output()`, and the LMCache worker-side buffer only moves on an engine step.
Evictions on the MP server — from other engines' stores on a shared server, from the server's own policy, from a restart — are invisible to the router until this engine next executes a step.
The router keeps sending prefix-affine requests to a placement that no longer exists.
Raised in #5307 review.
Not fixable in LMCache alone: the drain point is in vLLM.

### 4. The event path runs through the worker for no reason

Today: elected TP rank subscribes → worker buffer → `KVConnectorOutput` (or worker metadata under `MultiConnector`, #5524) → scheduler `update_connector_output()` → `take_events()`.
The subscription is a scheduler-side concern; the scheduler adapter already owns a request client and heartbeat per server.
The detour costs an extra hop per step, a TP aggregation rule (#5307 had to replace intersection with union), the #5524 carry, and a fallback to self-announced stores (#5076) — each a place where events get dropped, duplicated, or reordered.

### 5. SGLang has no event path

`UnifiedLMCacheMPConnector` exposes no events; `LMCacheUnifiedRadixCache.take_events()` returns only the GPU tree's. 
Dynamo/llm-d SGLang host-tier routing cannot see LMCache at all.

### Net effect

Ray Serve's offloading guide says that with LMCache the router scores an offloaded prefix as though it weren't cached.
llm-d's tiered-prefix-cache guide builds its CPU-tier index on vLLM-native events and lists LMCache with `lmcache:*` metrics only.
Both are accurate descriptions of what we ship.

| Problem | Closed by |
| --- | --- |
| 1. identity | PR 3, PR 4, PR 5 (vLLM); PR 6 + SGLang PR |
| 2. residency | PR 1 |
| 3. idle staleness | PR A + vLLM PR; SGLang already publishes on idle |
| 4. worker-side path | PR A |
| 5. SGLang | PR 6 + SGLang PR |

## Goal

Routers see the LMCache CPU tier with the engine's own block identities, at block granularity, only when a chunk is actually servable, on vLLM and SGLang, including while the engine is idle.
One code path.
When this lands, the Ray and llm-d notes above can be removed.

## Out of scope

- In-process mode. Its event bugs are tracked separately: #4543 (#4615), #5869.
- L2/STORAGE events and shared-tier placement ownership. Separate design; needs a publisher identity that is not an engine.
- cache_salt, LoRA, multimodal, sliding-window and hybrid models. Requests with these keep caching but carry no native bindings.
- Mixed worker/server versions. A mismatch fails at registration with an explicit error. There is no compatibility path.
- The chunk-hash events emitted today. They go away in PR A/PR 5. No fallback to them.

## Design

Server side
- `CommittedKVResidency` decides when a chunk is servable from CPU: every required `(kv_rank, object_group)` object has a committed readable copy on at least one L1 tag. Stored is emitted once on that transition; Removed once when the last copy of any required object is gone.
- Engines send a `KVEventProfile` at `register_kv_cache` and one `EventBinding` per complete chunk inside STORE: the engine's own block hashes, parent hash, tokens, block size. The server stores them and never reconstructs hashes.
- Records carry those identities. Replay log, incarnation and lost semantics are unchanged.

Engine side
- The subscription lives on the scheduler side (vLLM: `LMCacheMPSchedulerAdapter`; SGLang: the publisher rank's `UnifiedLMCacheMPConnector`), identified by a uuid instance id refreshed by PING. `take_events()` drains it directly. No worker-side event code, no TP aggregation, no `KVConnectorOutput` hop.
- vLLM publishes through its own KV-event publisher. Idle freshness needs a small vLLM change (linked below). SGLang already publishes on idle.
- Medium: the server records `CPU`; the vLLM connector emits `CPU`, the SGLang connector emits `StorageM

items.title: DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit
items.author: kahyunnam
items.body_excerpt:
# FlashInfer — DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit

**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Scope:** Audit of SM121 (compute capability 12.1, DGX Spark) support across FlashInfer ops, APIs, backends, and testing.
**Goal:** Improve Spark usability on FlashInfer by identifying existing gaps.

**Note: skip to "15. Consolidated Action Items" for TLDR.**

---

## Architecture Context

| Gencode | Target | CUDA Requirement |
|---------|--------|------------------|
| `compute_120a` / `sm_120a` | RTX 5090 (SM120) | CUDA 12.8 |
| `compute_120f` / `sm_120f` | SM12x family (120 + 121) | CUDA 12.9 |
| `compute_121a` / `sm_121a` | DGX Spark (SM121) | CUDA 12.9 |

### SM120 vs SM121: Implications for FlashInfer

Per the [CUDA 13.2 Programming Guide — Compute Capabilities](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html) (Tables 29–33), SM120 and SM121 share a single "12.x" spec column: identical shared memory (99 KB/block, 100 KB/SM), warps (48/SM), registers (64K/SM), tensor core data types (TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8), TMA, and cluster support. [Table 28](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html#compute-capabilities-family-specific-compatibility) confirms `compute_120f` is compatible with **both** CC 12.0 and 12.1. The chip-level differences (SM121 = aarch64 host, unified LPDDR5x, 84 SMs vs SM120's x86_64, discrete GDDR7, up to 170 SMs) do not affect kernel correctness — only SM-count-based heuristics and host toolchain.

### `f` vs `a` compilation targets: performance implications

Per the [PTX ISA 9.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html) (§9.7.15.5.14 for dense `mma`, §9.7.15.6.3 for sparse `mma.sp`), `120f` (family) is a subset of `120a`/`121a` (arch-specific). Most SM12x features — including **dense** NVFP4/MXFP4 block-scaled MMA — are family-specific and available via `120f` from PTX ISA 8.8. The arch-specific restriction (requiring `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`) applies **only to sparse MMA** (`mma.sp`) with `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4`:

| PTX Feature | `compute_120` (baseline) | `compute_120f` (family) | `compute_120a` / `compute_121a` (arch) |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| FP4/FP6/FP8 conversions (`cvt`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| FP4/FP6 MMA, block-scaled MMA (`.kind::mxf8f6f4`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Dense** NVFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Dense** MXFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** NVFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** MXFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |

FlashInfer's b12x GEMM kernel (`dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm120_b12x.py`) uses `cute.nvgpu.warp.MmaMXF4NVF4Op` — a **dense** block-scaled MMA atom. This means `sm_120f` wheels already emit native NVFP4/MXFP4 dense MMA instructions. Only **sparse** NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA (not currently used in FlashInfer) requires `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`.

> **Correction (2026-06-12):** An earlier version of this table stated that ALL `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4` MMA was arch-specific-only. Per [Harry-Chen's feedback](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3170#issuecomment-4677810517) and PTX ISA §9.7.15.5.14 vs §9.7.15.6.3, the restriction is limited to the sparse (`mma.sp`) variant.

### Wheel build arch targets

The release wheel CI (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) builds the following SM12x targets:

| CUDA Version | SM12x target in `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` |
|---|---|
| < 12.9 | `12.0a` (SM120 arch-specific; no SM121 support) |
| >= 12.9, < 13.0 | `12.0f` (family; covers SM120 + SM121; includes dense NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA) |
| >= 13.0 | `12.0f` (same) |

**No `121a` target is included in any wheel build.** However, since FlashInfer's FP4 kernels use **dense** block-scaled MMA (`MmaMXF4NVF4Op`, not sparse), the `120f` wheels already emit native NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA instructions. The `121a` target would only be needed for future sparse MMA kernels. JIT compilation on SM121 still produces `121a` cubins for forward-compatibility.

### What this means for FlashInfer

- **Any kernel that runs on SM120 is architecturally compatible with SM121.** Hardcoded `sm_version == "sm_120"` or `minor == 0` checks in backend dispatch are over-restricting without justification.
- **Separate cubins matter for JIT but not for wheels.** `CompilationContext` correctly emits `sm_121a` for JIT on SM121. Since FlashInfer uses only dense block-scaled MMA (available on `120f`), the wheels do not lose FP4 GEMM performance. The `121a` JIT path provides forward-compatibility for future sparse MMA use.
- **SMEM capacity maps, tile configs, and MMA atoms are identical.** Code using `get_smem_capacity_in_bytes("sm_120")` returns the correct value for SM121 too — the only risk is `KeyError` if a map expects an `"sm_121"` key and doesn't have one.

### Key utility functions

| Function (`utils.py`) | Behavior for SM121 |
|------------------------|--------------------|
| `is_sm12x_supported` | True (CUDA ≥ 12.9) |
| `is_sm121a_supported` | True (CUDA ≥ 12.9) |
| `is_sm120a_supported` | **False** (12.0 only) |
| `device_support_pdl` | True (`major >= 9`) |
| `determine_attention_backend` | Returns `fa2` (fa3 is SM90-only) |
| `determine_gemm_backend` | Returns `sm80` (no SM12x branch) |

---

## 1. Attention

### 1.1 Decode (batch paged KV)

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **fa2** | Generic | **Supported** | Default via `determine_attention_backend` for non-FP8 tensor-core decode |
| **fa3** | SM90 only | **Not available** | `determine_attention_backend` returns fa3 only on SM90 |
| **xqa** | `major in {9, 10, 12}` | **Supported** | `trtllm_batch_decode` auto → xqa when `major != 10` |
| **trtllm-gen** | `major == 10` only | **Not available** | Auto selects this

items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3-VL: rewriting video_metadata.total_num_frames without rescaling fps makes default HF frame sampling keep only min_frames and produces wrong `<t seconds>` timestamps
items.author: john-liu-dev
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc25 (`785c948`); transformers 5.5.4 (the version pinned in `requirements.txt`, also on `main`).
- Re-checked on `main` at `760a584` (2026-10-12): `_decide_do_sample_frames` and `Qwen3VLInputProcessorBase._preprocess` are identical to rc25 (main L169-221 and L349-425).
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` (the 8B model goes through the same code path).
- Seen end-to-end through the NVIDIA Dynamo TensorRT-LLM backend (`7e8b9fc2`) in aggregated multimodal mode; the reproduction below is CPU-only and needs only the HF processor.

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`Qwen3VLInputProcessorBase._preprocess` (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_qwen3vl.py`, L400-412 in rc25, L402-414 on `main`) forwards `VideoData.metadata` to the HF processor with `total_num_frames` rewritten to `len(vd.frames)`, so that HF's `sample_frames` (`np.linspace(0, total_num_frames - 1, num_frames)`) stays in range. The metadata `fps` (source video fps) and `frames_indices` are left untouched. When the IO layer has already subsampled the clip (e.g. 40 frames out of a 10 s / 24 fps / 240-frame video), HF's `Qwen3VLVideoProcessor` therefore believes the video is 40/24 = 1.67 s long and, with its class defaults (`fps=2`, `min_frames=4`), samples `int(40/24*2) = 3 -> 4` frames. This is the default path: when the caller passes no `do_sample_frames` / `num_frames` / `fps`, `_decide_do_sample_frames` (L167-219 in rc25, L169-221 on `main`) turns sampling on to match HF's class default. Two consequences:

1. Only 4 of the 40 decoded frames reach the ViT (1760 visual tokens instead of 11880). Any caller that does not pass `mm_processor_kwargs={"do_sample_frames": False}` (or an exact `num_frames`) silently gets a 4-frame summary of the video, regardless of clip length (a 30 s clip decoded to 40 frames gives the identical 4-frame result).
2. The `<t seconds>` timestamp tokens inserted by the processor are computed from the resampled indices over the rewritten `total_num_frames` divided by the *source* fps, so they are compressed by (decoded frames / source frames): for the 10 s clip the model sees `<0.3 seconds>` and `<1.4 seconds>` for frames that are actually at about 0 s, 3.3 s, 6.7 s and 10 s.

With `do_sample_frames=False` the processor uses `frames_indices / fps`, and both the frame count and the timestamps are correct, which shows the frame list itself is fine; only the sampling-path metadata is inconsistent. For comparison, HF sampling the 240-frame source itself at the default fps=2 would keep `int(240/24*2) = 20` frames with timestamps in source seconds, so the rewrite also makes the default path diverge from stock HF, which `_decide_do_sample_frames` intends to match.

Reproduction (CPU only, HF processor only):

- Decode a 10 s, 24 fps, 1280x720 H.264 clip into 40 uniformly spaced RGB float32 `(C, H, W)` tensors in [0, 1], metadata = `{"fps": 24.0, "total_num_frames": 240, "duration": 10.0, "frames_indices": linspace(0, 239, 40)}`.
- Apply the same rewrite as `_preprocess` (`total_num_frames := 40`) and call `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct")(text=[chat_template_text], videos=[frames], video_metadata=[meta], do_sample_frames=True, do_rescale=False, padding=True, return_tensors="pt")`.
- Observe `video_grid_thw == [2, 44, 80]`, 1760 `<|video_pad|>` tokens, timestamps `<0.3 seconds>`, `<1.4 seconds>`.
- Same call with `do_sample_frames=False`: `video_grid_thw == [20, 36, 66]`, 11880 tokens, timestamps `<0.1 seconds>`, `<0.6 seconds>`, `<1.1 seconds>`, `<1.6 seconds>`, ... (one per 0.5 s across the clip).
- Without the rewrite (original `total_num_frames=240`) HF raises `IndexError: index 50 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 40`, which confirms why the rewrite exists.
- End-to-end: the Dynamo TensorRT-LLM worker's `/metrics` reports `trtllm_prompt_tokens_total = 1789` (= 1760 visual + 4 vision markers + 12 timestamp tokens + 13 text) for this request.

### Expected behavior

Either (a) when rewriting `total_num_frames` to the decoded count, also rescale `fps` to `len(frames) / duration` and reset `frames_indices` to `range(len(frames))`, so HF's duration and timestamps stay consistent with the frames it receives, or (b) default `do_sample_frames` to False whenever the caller passes an already-subsampled frame list with `frames_indices` (the IO layer has done the sampling), and only sample when the caller explicitly asks for `num_frames` / `fps`.

### actual behavior

With default `mm_processor_kwargs`, 4 of 40 decoded frames reach the ViT and the timestamps are compressed by 40/240 (details under Reproduction).

### additional notes

**Impact.** Silent quality loss for every video request that relies on defaults (temporal reasoning over a ~2 s window of a longer clip, wrong timestamps), plus misleading throughput numbers (the prompt is ~7x shorter than intended).

**Workaround.** Pass `mm_processor_kwargs={"do_sample_frames": False}` per request (the frame count is then whatever the IO layer decoded, e.g. `DYN_MM_VIDEO_NUM_FRAMES` in Dynamo).

The metadata rewrite and `_decide_do_sample_frames` were introduced in #15598.

**Related:** #20138 (Qwen3-VL video over the E/PD handoff; its reproduction passes `do_sample_frames=False` to get all decoded frames into the ViT, i.e. the workaround above).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the [documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM/) and [examples](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/examples) for answers to frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Feature]: Add request-level dynamic batching to VisualGen
items.author: yanxinzhangcs
items.body_excerpt:
### Feature, motivation and pitch

Add opt-in request-level dynamic batching to VisualGen. Independent concurrent image-generation requests currently execute as separate pipeline calls. Short image sequences can leave GPU capacity available, so combining compatible queued requests can improve throughput.

Expose `VisualGenArgs.batching_config` consistently in Python and serving YAML, with a generated-image batch cap and a bounded queue collection delay. Keep independent execution as the default. Preserve each caller's request ID, seed/noise stream and outputs, and run unsupported pipelines or request configurations independently.

Initial scope: FLUX.1/FLUX.2 text-to-image and unquantized, single-GPU Qwen-Image with VANILLA attention. Requests share a complete denoising run; new arrivals join the next pipeline execution. Include singleton/golden image quality comparisons and end-to-end serving benchmarks.

### Alternatives

Callers can manually combine prompts in one request, but that does not batch independent requests arriving through the serving API and leaves batching and result routing to clients.

### Additional context

The proposed implementation includes numerical safeguards for Qwen's request-shape-sensitive BF16 operations, regression tests, serving configuration and documentation.

items.title: [BUG] 02_dump_reg_shmem faults on sm_120: Fragment is 2-byte aligned but accessed through a 16-byte-aligned pointer
items.author: random25160765-collab
items.body_excerpt:
> **Correction (2026-09-13).** My original report framed this as an `nvcc` codegen bug specific to
> `sm_120`. That framing was wrong, and I have rewritten this issue. Further testing showed the
> codegen is identical on `sm_80`/`sm_90`/`sm_100`/`sm_120`, and that the underlying defect is on the
> CUTLASS side: the iterators access `Fragment` through a type that requires 16-byte alignment, while
> `Fragment` itself is only 2-byte aligned. Details and a verified fix below.

## Summary

`examples/02_dump_reg_shmem` aborts on `sm_120` with `cudaErrorMisalignedAddress` (error 716); the
example prints `Failed` and exits `255`. Reproduced on `main` @ `147295a3` with the stock example.

Root cause: `PredicatedTileIterator` reinterprets its `Fragment` (a plain `cutlass::Array`, 2-byte
aligned for `half_t`) as a 16-byte-aligned `AlignedArray` and accesses it 128 bits at a time. When the
compiler homes that fragment in local memory, it allocates the frame slot using the *declared*
alignment (2 → offset `+0xc`) but emits the stores using the *cast-implied* alignment (16 →
`STL.128`). The slot ends up at `12 (mod 16)`, so the 16-byte store is misaligned and the kernel
faults. Aligning the fragment moves the slot to `+0x10` and the example completes.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060, compute capability 12.0 (`sm_120`), driver 591.86 |
| Toolkit | CUDA 13.3 — nvcc V13.3.73 (`cuda_13.3.r13.3/compiler.38244171_0`) |
| OS | Linux (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS under WSL2), x86_64 |
| CUTLASS | `main` @ `147295a3`, unmodified (`git status` clean) |

## Where the alignment requirement comes from

The example itself is not at fault — `examples/02_dump_reg_shmem/dump_reg_shmem.cu:85` only declares

```cpp
typename GmemIterator::Fragment frag;
```

The requirement is imposed by the iterator
(`include/cutlass/transform/threadblock/predicated_tile_iterator.h`):

| Line | Code | Alignment |
|---|---|---|
| [181](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/main/include/cutlass/transform/threadblock/predicated_tile_iterator.h#L181) | `using AccessType = AlignedArray<Element, AccessSize, (AccessSize * sizeof_bits<Element>::value / 8)>;` | **16 bytes** (for `half_t`, `AccessSize == 8`) |
| [191](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/main/include/cutlass/transform/threadblock/predicated_tile_iterator.h#L191) | `using Fragment = cutlass::Array<Element, ThreadMap::Iterations::kCount * ThreadMap::kElementsPerAccess>;` | **2 bytes** — `cutlass::Array` has no `alignas` (`include/cutlass/array.h:101`; only `AlignedArray` at `array.h:2867` declares one) |
| [327](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/main/include/cutlass/transform/threadblock/predicated_tile_iterator.h#L327) | `AccessType *frag_ptr = reinterpret_cast<AccessType *>(&frag);` | casts the 2-byte-aligned object to the 16-byte-aligned type |

So the library relies on an alignment its own `Fragment` type does not declare. That dependency is
invisible to a caller who simply declares `typename GmemIterator::Fragment frag;`, which is the
documented idiom — and it is the reason the example breaks without any misuse on the caller's side.

## Evidence

**SASS of `kernel_dump` (`cuobjdump -sass`), stock example — the local slot is at `+0xc`:**

```sass
STL.128 [R1+0xc], R52 ;
STL.128 [R1+0x1c], R48 ;
STL.128 [R1+0x2c], R44 ;
STL.128 [R1+0x3c], R40 ;
STL.128 [R1+0x4c], R36 ;
STL.128 [R1+0x5c], R32 ;
STL.128 [R1+0x6c], R28 ;
STL.128 [R1+0x7c], R24 ;
```

Every offset is `≡ 12 (mod 16)`; `STL.128` requires a 16-byte-aligned address, and the kernel faults
at the first one.

**With the fragment aligned, the slot moves and the fault disappears:**

| | fragment slot | `STL.128` offsets | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| stock | `+0xc` | `0xc, 0x1c, … 0x7c` (all `≡12 mod 16`) | fault, exit 255 |
| `alignas(16)` | `+0x10` | `0x10, 0x20, … 0x80` (all 16-byte aligned) | **completes, exit 0** |

**Not architecture-specific.** Compiling the reproducer below for `sm_80`, `sm_90`, `sm_100` and
`sm_120` produces the identical 8 × `STL.128` at `[R1+0xc … R1+0x7c]`. The codegen is
architecture-independent; whether it faults depends on the runtime frame base, and on `sm_120` it
does. (I could only *execute* on `sm_120` — other architectures were compile-only.)

## Proposed fix

Minimal, verified on `sm_120`:

```cpp
// examples/02_dump_reg_shmem/dump_reg_shmem.cu:85
alignas(16) typename GmemIterator::Fragment frag;
```

However this only protects the example. Since `AccessType` is 16-byte aligned for every user of
`PredicatedTileIterator` (and the other iterators with the same pattern), the more principled fix
would be to declare the alignment on the `Fragment` typedef itself — e.g. make it an `AlignedArray`,
or add `alignas` — so that any caller declaring `Fragment frag;` is safe. That is a wider change, so
I'd rather leave the choice to the maintainers.

## Exposure (why this is not caught elsewhere)

A fragment that never has its address taken stays in registers and never touches local memory. Real
GEMM kernels therefore don't hit this. The fault needs the fragment's address to escape to a
non-inlined function — which is exactly what the dump/debug path does (`cutlass::debug::dump_fragment`,
`printf`). That is consistent with it showing up in this example and seemingly nowhere else.

## Note on the compiler side

I filed this with NVIDIA's compiler team as well. Their assessment was that the
`reinterpret_cast` to a 16-byte-aligned type is a source-level alignment promise that the object does
not satisfy, and therefore source-level UB rather than a codegen defect. I accept that reading — it
is why I have rewritten this issue rather than insisting on a compiler bug. The remaining point for
CUTLASS is narrower: the library should not depend on an alignment guarantee its own type does not
make.

<summary>Minimal reproducer (no CUTLASS)</summary>

The program below reproduces the same codegen and fault on `sm_120`. Note that the `Frame` layout is
deliberately constructe

items.title: [BUG] Instantiated tile sizes for sm120 fail to meet kernel's layout assertion during cutlass_profiler compile
items.author: CYQFWang
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CUTLASS C++

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

`make cutlass_profiler -j8` fails with the following log. 
The log suggests the generated tile sizes for the kernel cannot meet a layout assertion.

items.title: [Feature][Rubin] KCP: precise state passing and ragged per-document zigzag
items.author: abcdabcd987
items.body_excerpt:
## Problem

We need Kimi Context Parallel (KCP) training for KDA: keep tokens local and exchange recurrent-state summaries instead of redistributing tokens/heads. Extend CAKE's existing packed KDA backend, whose public contract currently starts each document from zero without cross-rank state handling ([current contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/366214d4325e049199c9e79aa1eb30b0d3a867f1/flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_train/README.md)).

The main gaps are the cost of accurate state propagation and support for per-document zigzag. FLA's current zigzag partitions the whole packed buffer rather than each document ([context builder](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/9d478facb282410dc150051d5f57205cd3812f31/fla/ops/cp/context.py#L128-L207)). For numerical accuracy, use TF32x3/FP32 as the baseline rather than plain-TF32 affine products; [FLA #1546](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/pull/1546) already addresses the precision policy, so the goal here is to make the accurate path efficient.

## Requested outcome

- **Precise state passing, forward and backward:** Optimize affine-summary construction, cross-rank merge, and reverse-state propagation, including downstream-shard contributions to earlier tokens. Match the qualified TF32x3/FP32 path's accuracy; FP32 storage with plain-TF32 products is not sufficient.

- **Per-document zigzag and ragged partitions:** Support multiple fragments per rank in document order, not merely two intervals of the whole packed buffer. Carry state across CP cuts and reset at true document boundaries. Accept unequal counts and partial chunks; native segmented handling or an efficient layout adapter is acceptable, with all costs included.

- **Compact boundary-state buffers:** Store only needed continuation states and adjoints. Avoid mostly-zero per-sequence state expansion and gathered-summary `cat/flip` copies; size and report storage/communication by actual crossing fragments.

- **Checkpoint and convolution integration:** Support saved-context backward and checkpoint replay. Provide width-4 causal-convolution halo/gradient integration without full activation concatenations, preserving FP32 SiLU preactivations for backward; convolution fusion is not required.

## Target hardware

Required targets: **`sm_100`, `sm_103`, and `sm_107`**. Qualify correctness and performance separately on each; the benchmark below covers GB200 only.

Use multi-GPU groups within one NVLink domain, including groups spanning hosts. Inter-rack communication is outside the initial scope.

## Inference engine

PyTorch native / custom training integration. This is forward/backward training with activation checkpointing, not inference-only prefill.

## Workload and configuration

The reference workload is GLM-5.3-Flash KDA: **64 heads, key/value dimensions 128**, and module hidden width 4096. Start with CP2/4/8/16; each token-sharded rank retains all heads.

| Operand | Reference shape | Dtype / meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `q`, `k`, `v`, `out`, `dout` | `[1,T_r,64,128]` | BF16; Q/K already L2-normalized and stored in BF16 |
| `g` | `[1,T_r,64,128]` | FP32, preactivated natural-log decay; `safe_gate=True`, lower bound −5 |
| `beta` | `[1,T_r,64]` | BF16, already sigmoid-activated |
| State and transition summary | Each `[64,128,128]` per crossing fragment | FP32; logically `S_out = M @ S_in + B` |
| Partition metadata | Variable-size document/fragment tables | True document boundaries, local ranges, and predecessor/successor ownership |
| Convolution boundary | Input `[T_r,8192]`, weights `[8192,4]` | BF16 input, FP32 weights; up to three history rows per continuation |

`dq/dk/dv/dbeta` follow the BF16 input-storage boundary; `dg` remains FP32. Keep external normalization and gate construction compatible with the existing training contract.

**`T_r` is irregular, need not be a power of two or chunk multiple, and varies across ranks and runs.** Cover unequal documents, short/empty fragments, document boundaries inside chunks, and documents spanning at least three shards; no tail dropping or cross-document state leakage.

Reference packs contain about 226K–262K total tokens and 2–6 documents, with document lengths about 23K–131K. Include a 249,856-token pack in benchmarks; these are representative workloads, not fixed kernel dimensions.

## Current workaround

Use head-parallel redistribution plus local KDA, or FLA TF32x3 KCP with custom halos and contiguous/global-zigzag partitions. Neither gives an optimized per-document-zigzag KCP path directly.

For scale, a GB200 benchmark using CP16, 249,856 packed tokens, 64 heads, and 128-dimensional keys/values measured **32.0 ms for TF32x3 KCP versus 37.4 ms for optimized head CP**, both using contiguous partitions and module forward+backward timing. This used FLA revision `9d478facb282410dc150051d5f57205cd3812f31`; it does not establish the cost of a per-document layout adapter or a comparison against the newer CAKE local KDA backend.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Numerics:** Check output and all five input gradients against FP64 and no-CP BF16 references on identical inputs. Calibrate per-tensor budgets; include slow-decay/anisotropic-key cases that reject the plain-TF32 regression. Require repeatability, not bitwise equality to no-CP.
- **Semantics:** Test actual multi-GPU execution, per-document zigzag, uneven tails, boundary resets, halo gradients, and direct versus checkpointed backward. All gradients, including `dg` and `dbeta`, must have hard acceptance gates rather than warning-only checks.
- **Performance and memory:** Beat qualified FLA KCP on representative shapes without increasing peak memory; also compare with the best qualified CAKE head-CP path. Include collectives, conversions, halos, copies, and replay. Report slowest-rank latency, workspace/retained state, and cold-start versus steady-state peaks.

## Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

Build on [CAKE packed KDA #6

items.title: [Bug] b12x fused_moe w4a8_mx deterministic_output=True: wrong outputs with dynamic_tile_m=32 and with masked (-1) routes
items.author: thenaxon
items.body_excerpt:
b12x 1.5.1, `fused_moe` (`w4a8_mx`, dynamic backend) with `Caps(deterministic_output=True)` gives wrong outputs in two cases. `deterministic_output=False` is correct for the same inputs in both. Related: #6941 (deterministic_output with direct routing).

**1. `dynamic_tile_m == 32` is wrong.** The planner also picks this with `decode_config=None`.

- Top-6, K=5120, n=2048, E=16 at 5–64 tokens per call: cosine against `deterministic_output=False` is about 0.
- Same for E=96 at 65–512 tokens.
- `dynamic_tile_m` 64 and 128 are correct.

**2. Masked routes are not zero-filled with `dynamic_route_mode='grouped'`** (the only mode `deterministic_output` accepts).

- For routes with `topk_ids == -1`, the per-route output rows are not written. The top-k-sum combine then adds stale per-route scratch from earlier calls.
- Cosine against `deterministic_output=False` is 0.5–0.85, and rows whose routes are all -1 come out non-zero.
- A fresh plan's first call is clean; later calls are wrong.
- Expert-parallel integrations mask non-local experts with -1, so this hits every EP rank.

**Repro**

- Random weights. Dirty the scratch with one call, then call again with about 60 % of `topk_ids` set to -1.
- Compare against the same call with `deterministic_output=False`, or with the masked routes replaced by (expert 0, weight 0).

**Environment:** b12x 1.5.1, SM120 (RTX 5090), CUDA 13.2, driver 595.

**Workaround:** use `dynamic_tile_m >= 64` for deterministic plans, and remap masked routes to a local expert with weight 0. With both, a sweep over E 12/16/96 and T 1–2100, masked and unmasked, matches the non-deterministic path.

items.title: KV cache L2 get with mget counts blocks after a missing block, so the caller uses an unfilled block as KV cache
items.author: wguo7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`L2Cache.get()` returns a block count, and the caller treats the first that many memory regions as blocks 0 to n-1 of the sequence. `KVCacheManager` takes `mrs[:value]` as fetched and also puts them into L1 under those blocks' keys ([cache_manager.py#L1340-L1368](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/cache_manager.py#L1340-L1368)).

On a backend with the `mput_mget` feature, `get()` goes through `_mget_impl()` and `_backend_mget_impl()`. The latter counts every block whose status reports success, and on a miss or a token mismatch it moves on to the next block instead of stopping ([l2_cache.py#L576-L588](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/l2/l2_cache.py#L576-L588)). With block 1 of 4 missing, it returns 3, and the caller takes blocks 0, 1 and 2, where block 1 is a region the backend never wrote. In addition, `_mget_impl()` adds the next batch's count after a batch that came back short ([l2_cache.py#L521-L543](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/l2/l2_cache.py#L521-L543)), so a miss at the end of one batch is counted past in the same way.

The path without mget, `_get_impl()`, stops at the first miss ([l2_cache.py#L612-L618](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/l2/l2_cache.py#L612-L618)), and so does `exists()`. The SHFS connector always enables mget ([shfs.py#L74](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/l2/connectors/shfs.py#L74)), and MOCK and PrisKV enable it through `AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_MOCK_USE_MPUT_MGET` and `AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_PRISKV_USE_MPUT_MGET` ([envs.py#L96](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/envs.py#L96), [envs.py#L134](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/envs.py#L134)). A gap appears when one block of a sequence is lost while the others stay: a file removed from the shared directory, a put that failed on one block of a batch (SHFS `mput()` keeps writing the blocks after a failed one, [shfs.py#L160-L174](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/l2/connectors/shfs.py#L160-L174)), or a key evicted by the backend. Token validation is off by default (`AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_TOKEN_VALIDATION_ENABLED`, [envs.py#L197-L199](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/envs.py#L197-L199)), so nothing else rejects the unfilled block.

### Steps to Reproduce

The script puts 4 blocks through `L2Cache` (block i filled with the value i + 1), deletes block 1 from the backend, and gets the 4 blocks into regions filled with -1. It runs on SHFS (a temporary directory) and on MOCK with mget on. Output on main (f3300be):

```
[SHFS] put -> 4 blocks
[SHFS] exists -> 1 blocks
